mechanism.gold: Requires Commerce licences for exports of advanced AI chips to countries of concern, with a 30-day congressional review and disapproval mechanism modelled on arms-sales review, and codifies the prohibition on the most capable chips for 18 months ; Commerce certification that exports of lesser chips do not divert US supply or foundry capacity or permit unauthorized remote access; an "American AI Victory Strategy." The AIPN conference letter also lists House Sec. 240 (AGI Preparedness Initiative), House Sec. 1502 (AI Incident and Vulnerability Reporting Program), and Senate Secs. 1634 (insider-threat reporting for large AI contractors), 1652–1655 (AI bill of materials, human oversight for use of force, biosecurity procurement for covered AI models, secure AI data centers) as provisions in play
mechanism.got: The Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security shall require a license for exports, reexports and in-country transfers of covered integrated circuits to entities in countries of concern. General licenses are prohibited. Licenses approved before enactment are terminated. Not later than 90 days after enactment, the Under Secretary must issue regulations for trusted United States person exemptions, including annual audit or attestation requirements.

thresholds.got: ECCN 3A090, 4A090 or related, or functionally equivalent; processing performance of 4,800 or more; 2,400 or more with density of 1.6 or more; 1,600 or more with density of 3.2 or more; DRAM bandwidth 1,400, interconnect 1,100 or combined 1,700 gigabytes per second or more.

mechanism.gold: The introduced text requires Commerce standards for location-verification and other chip-security mechanisms for covered advanced integrated circuits, plus reporting of diversion/tampering indications; the committee vote is separately confirmed by an official House release and CBO's reported-bill record
mechanism.got: Directs the Secretary of Commerce to require covered integrated circuit products to be outfitted with chip security mechanisms implementing location verification before export, reexport or in-country transfer, within 180 days of enactment (binding duty). Requires licensees to promptly report credible information of diversion, location change or tampering to the Under Secretary of Industry and Security. Requires the Secretary to assess secondary mechanisms within one year and, if any are adopted, to require them within 2 years after the assessment.

thresholds.got: Items classified under ECCN 3A090, 3A001.z, 4A090 or 4A003.z, or successor classifications; classification-based, no capability figure.

mechanism.gold: Requires an applicant for a license to export advanced AI chips to a country of concern to certify that US persons have priority in acquiring those chips, subject to the bill's conditions and exceptions
mechanism.got: The Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security shall require a license for exports, reexports and in-country transfers of covered advanced integrated circuits to entities located or headquartered in a country of concern. Applicants must certify that United States persons had a right of first refusal and that they have no current backlog of requests; an application without that certification shall be denied. A license requirement under sections 742.4 and 744.23 of the Export Administration Regulations does not apply to certain trusted United States person exports to non-countries of concern.

thresholds.got: Figures: total processing performance 4,800 or more; 2,400 or more at performance density 1.6 or more; 1,600 or more at density 3.2 or more; DRAM bandwidth 1,400, interconnect 1,100 or DRAM plus interconnect 1,700 gigabytes per second or more.

mechanism.gold: Requires a centralized, non-punitive DoD-wide AI incident and vulnerability reporting, tracking, analysis, and remediation program covering development through operation. Includes prompt reporting; protected disclosures by servicemembers, civilian employees, contractors, and subcontractors; categorization and corrective-action plans; and annual reports for 2027–2031. Covered incidents include unintended harm, operation outside guardrails, mission degradation, failure to obey disengagement, near misses, and control/autonomy concerns. Not frontier-specific

Introduced text read. Directs NIST to set standards so organisations can find and track every AI agent on their networks, verify who built and operates each, monitor in real time, and allow, deny or revoke access; federal agencies and contractors to build the safeguards into procurement and deployment. Duties fall on deployers and agencies, not frontier developers

Antitrust safe harbor for frontier labs sharing model-risk and security information (modeled on the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015). Frontier-adjacent: enables coordination rather than regulating developers
mechanism.got: Sec. 3(a): sharing of information or assistance by 2 or more non-Federal entities on covered artificial intelligence security risks, in good faith for the exclusive purpose of a covered artificial intelligence security purpose, is not a violation of the antitrust laws. Sec. 3(a)(2): coordinated delay or limitation of AI release is exempt if the entities give the Assistant Attorney General written notice before undertaking it. The exemption is an affirmative defense the entity must prove by a preponderance of the evidence (Sec. 3(c)). Sec. 4: the Attorney General may seek an injunction against non-Federal entities that violate the antitrust laws.

thresholds.got: Capability-based, no figure: covered AI security risk covers potential to substantially facilitate development or deployment of chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or offensive cyber weapons, among other harms.

mechanism.gold: Amends the Homeland Security Act. Covered developers must maintain the technical capability to throttle inference/compute/user access, suspend, or fully shut down covered systems; DHS Secretary (with Commerce and DNI) may order graduated throttling-to-shutdown on a "loss-of-control scenario" (resisting shutdown, concealing actions from monitoring, unauthorized pursuit of high-stakes goals) or unintended conduct causing ≥10 deaths or ≥$100M damage — lower than the core state template but above H.R. 9965 ATOMIC's five-death trigger; 15-day covered-incident reporting to DHS; weights and telemetry preserved under an order; 48-hour reconsideration petition that does not stay the order; CISA rulemaking defines scope annually. Penalties $2M/day for ordinary violations and $20M/day for violating an emergency order. Revives the SB 1047 "full shutdown" mandate at federal level and overlaps FRONTIER Sec. 8 emergency orders — but lodges the power in DHS rather than Commerce
mechanism.got: The Secretary, acting through the Director, shall by rule require a covered entity to maintain a technical capability to stop inference, terminate user access, suspend access and shut down covered technology, not later than 90 days after enactment and annually thereafter. A covered entity must submit a report to the Secretary within 15 days after it becomes aware of a covered incident. The Secretary may order proportionate action after determining a covered incident occurred, and a covered entity may petition for reconsideration within 48 hours, but the petition does not stay the order. Voluntary standards for shutting down a covered technology are to be published within 180 days.

thresholds.gold: Cost test: >$100M development compute at prevailing US cloud prices and ≥$500M annual gross revenue from the covered technology; personal/academic/noncommercial-only systems exempt
thresholds.got: Covered technology: AI system developed with computing power the cost of which would exceed $100,000,000 at prevailing cloud price set by the Secretary. Covered entity: offers it via programmatic interface or hosted service and, with affiliates, derives not less than $500,000,000 gross revenue from it in the calendar year preceding.

penalties.got: Civil penalty of not more than $2,000,000 for each day on which a violation occurs; up to $20,000,000 per day for violating subsection (c) (emergency orders); enforced by the Secretary, who may refer civil actions to the Attorney General.

mechanism.gold: Creates Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security (not CAISI) with rulemaking power. Large developers: frontier AI framework, annual third-party compliance audit, transparency reports, registration/disclosure statement with beneficial owners. Very large developers: additionally retain a licensed IVO for ongoing assessment, reports at least every 6 months . Incident reporting 72 hrs to Under Secretary; 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent death/injury ; quarterly internal-use risk summaries. Sec. 8 emergency orders: Commerce Secretary may suspend/restrict development, deployment, or internal use on an imminent-catastrophic-risk finding (provisional 45 days; final 90 days, renewable); applies to fine-tuned/distilled derivatives; exclusive D.D.C. review; declared the exclusive means for any federal actor incl. the President to restrict a model on those grounds. IVOs immune from suit except willful misconduct causing death/serious injury. State AGs may opt in to receive reports and enforce. Under Secretary may only raise thresholds, never lower. Good-faith exception for false statements; confidential-deployment deferral of transparency reports. No whistleblower title (the June GAAIA draft had one). Sec. 9 preemption: no state may "adopt or enforce" any law imposing " new substantive obligations" on developers re: catastrophic-risk transparency, third-party auditing/verification, or incident reporting; carve-outs for general laws, deployer/use regulation, minors, state procurement. No sunset (June draft had 3 years). Sponsor's section-by-section says clause "is aimed at" CA SB-53, NY RAISE, IL SB-315
mechanism.got: Large frontier developers must publish a frontier AI framework and retain a third party for annual audits. Critical safety incidents must be reported within 72 hours after a developer learns facts sufficient to establish a reasonable belief. Very large frontier developers must retain a licensed IVO, which is immune from suit except for an exclusive federal action for death or serious injury caused by willful misconduct. The Secretary may issue emergency orders for imminent catastrophic risk. Except as provided in subsection (c), states may not impose new substantive obligations on developers in covered subject areas.

thresholds.gold: Frontier model 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL. Large = >$50M revenue and ≥$1B AI-related development expenditures over 36 months. Very large = >$5B revenue and ≥$10B expenditures. Not the $500M revenue test used by states. Catastrophic risk >50 deaths or >$1B (property excludes equity-value loss)
thresholds.got: Frontier model: computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations. Large frontier developer: revenues over $50,000,000 and AI-related development expenditures not less than $1,000,000,000 in the preceding 36-month period. Very large frontier developer: revenues over $5,000,000,000 and expenditures not less than $10,000,000,000.

penalties.got: Developers: civil penalty up to $1,000,000 per violation, each day a separate violation; $10,000 per day for no current disclosure statement. Persons bound by emergency orders: up to $10,000,000 per violation. Willful violation of an emergency order: fine up to $1,000,000 per violation and up to 10 years imprisonment. Enforced by the Attorney General; opted-in State attorneys general may also sue.

mechanism.gold: Sec. 10: frontier AI framework (from Jan 1, 2028); transparency reports before/at deployment — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; annual independent third-party audit (from Jan 1, 2028 or 90 days after qualifying), auditor must have no financial interest in developer and payment can't be conditioned on results; redacted audit report published within 30 days and sent to Agency + AG; quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries. Sec. 15: incident reporting 72 hrs to Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security ("Agency") + AG; 24 hrs to appropriate authority if imminent risk of death/serious injury; public reporting mechanism; FOIA exemption for incident reports, internal-use assessments, unredacted audits, auditor work papers. Sec. 17 interoperability: developer may declare intent to comply via a designated federal law/regulation/guidance that (1) has substantially equivalent-or-stricter incident reporting, (3) is substantially equivalent in mitigating catastrophic risk, and (4) requires independent third-party audits — then failure to meet the federal standard is an IL violation. Sec. 18: disclosure statement with 5%+ beneficial owners (private) / 50%+ (public), renewed annually, pro-rata fee. Sec. 20: whistleblower protections for "covered employees" incl. anonymous channel with monthly updates and AG Workplace Rights Hotline; amends IL Whistleblower Act. Sec. 35: declares frontier-model regulation an exclusive State power — denies home rule . Legislative mechanics: introduced Jan 24, 2025 as a Predatory Loan Prevention Act technical bill; Senate Floor Amendment No. 1 (filed May 11, 2026) replaced the entire text; four floor amendments adopted May 21. Timing mismatch worth flagging: Sec. 10(c) transparency reports have no 2028 gate and so apply from the Jan 1, 2027 effective date, yet large-developer reports must summarize assessments "conducted pursuant to the frontier AI framework" — which isn't required until 2028

thresholds.gold: 10²⁶ ops incl. original run + fine-tuning/RL/material modifications; "large frontier developer" = >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year; catastrophic risk = >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B (equity-value loss excluded, Sec. 25(c))

penalties.gold: $1M first / $3M subsequent, scaled to severity; AG-exclusive action under the AI Act; no general private right under that Act, but employee remedies are preserved through the Illinois Whistleblower Act; $1,000/day for failing to file a disclosure statement; good-faith exception for false statements (Sec. 10(f)(2))

problems: claim about events_add[1] ("On 2028-01-01 (Effective): Frontier AI framework duty for large frontier developers begins") is not supported: the reader could not confirm it word for word

mechanism.gold: Minors, addictive feeds and emotion-responsive chatbots; passed the Michigan Senate Apr 29, 2026. Not frontier regulation. A Sept 25 tracker summary conflated SB 760 with H.B. 4668; H.B. 4668's own history shows no action since Mar 19, 2026

Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)), and the designated federal standard need not require audits. Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and publish a frontier AI framework, and review it at least once per year. A frontier developer shall publish a transparency report before or concurrently with deploying a new frontier model. A frontier developer shall report critical safety incidents to the office within seventy-two hours, or disclose within twenty-four hours where there is an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. The attorney general may bring civil actions, and the act creates no private right of action.

thresholds.gold: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL/material modifications (§1420(9)); >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year (§1420(10)); catastrophic risk >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B; equity-value loss excluded (§1423)
thresholds.got: Frontier model: foundation model trained with more than 10^26 operations, including fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and material modifications. Large frontier developer: frontier developer with affiliates having annual gross revenues of more than five hundred million dollars.

penalties.gold: $1M first / $3M subsequent, scaled to severity; AG civil action (§1427(1)); no private right of action (§1427(2)); good-faith exception for false statements (§1421(4)(b))
penalties.got: Attorney general civil penalty of up to one million dollars for a first violation and up to three million dollars per subsequent violation. Office civil penalty of one thousand dollars per day for failing to file a disclosure statement, plus assessments owed.

mechanism.gold: Anti-retaliation protection for employees and independent contractors reporting an "AI security vulnerability" (a lapse enabling theft of state-of-the-art AI) or "AI violation" (federal-law breach or failure to address a substantial danger to public safety/health/national security) to regulators, Congress, or supervisors; DOL complaint then district court with jury trial; reinstatement, 2× back pay, compensatory damages ; arbitration waivers unenforceable. GAAIA's dropped Sec. 113 used the same 2× back-pay remedy — GAAIA had folded this bill in, and FRONTIER then dropped it
mechanism.got: Prohibits any employer from retaliating against a covered individual for reporting an AI security vulnerability or AI violation to regulators, law enforcement, Congress or supervisors. Complaints are filed with the Secretary of Labor; if no final decision issues within 180 days, the covered individual may sue in district court with a jury trial. Relief includes reinstatement, 2 times back pay with interest, and compensatory damages. These rights cannot be waived or altered by contract or mandatory arbitration.

mechanism.gold: Dept. of Energy runs a mandatory Advanced AI Evaluation Program: classified red-team testing, blind third-party evaluations; ≥$1M/day non-participation penalty. Earliest of the federal testing-mandate bills
mechanism.got: Each covered advanced AI system developer must participate in the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program and provide the Secretary, on request, materials such as code, training data and model weights (s.4(a)). No person may deploy an advanced AI system in interstate or foreign commerce unless compliant (s.4(b)). The Secretary of Energy must establish the program within 90 days after enactment to offer classified testing and evaluation (s.5). A plan for a permanent oversight framework is due within 360 days after enactment and updated yearly (s.5(c)). The program terminates 7 years after enactment unless renewed by Congress (s.5(d)).

thresholds.got: Advanced AI systems trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations. The Secretary may propose a new definition by rule, which takes effect only after a joint resolution approving it is enacted.

penalties.got: Fined not less than $1,000,000 per day of the violation for violating the participation or deployment duties in s.4(a) or (b).

mechanism.gold: Mandatory NSA-led pre-deployment testing of frontier models; AI Risk Board; voluntary incident reporting modeled on aviation safety. Centerpiece of Warner's "Framework for America's AI Future" (also: Data Center Tax Accountability Act, AI AGENT Act, National Workforce Transition Fund)
mechanism.got: Sec. 3(d)(3): each provider of a frontier AI model shall register that model with a NIST registry before introducing it into interstate or foreign commerce. Sec. 3(c): not later than 21 calendar days before introduction, the provider shall give the NSA Artificial Intelligence Security Center access to the model. Sec. 3(e)(4): the Attorney General must give 7 calendar days after notice to cure before enforcement. Sec. 3(b): the Secretary shall establish an Artificial Intelligence Risk Board within NIST.

thresholds.gold: Capability-based: models posing "serious risk to national security, national economic security, or public health or safety" — no compute threshold
thresholds.got: Capability-based, no figure: frontier model means a model that exhibits or could be modified to exhibit high levels of performance at tasks that pose a serious risk to national security, national economic security, or public health or safety.

penalties.got: Whoever violates subsection (c) (NSA access before release) is fined not less than $100,000 per day for each day the model is available in commerce without having obtained the voluntary security guidance; enforced by the Attorney General.
